result:
Changed the request to a single fluent noun phrase; kept indirect (non-naming) identification.

New request: "Please set the 'Login fails on checkout' issue to High priority. It is in the private PAY* team that handles checkout billing." Seed, query, decoys, and write are unchanged — "PAY*" still maps to the contains-PAY key filter, and "handles checkout billing" still maps to the description-substring filter, so every decoy still fails exactly one condition.

On the reader's "just name it (Payments/PAY)" suggestion: I kept indirect identification deliberately, because naming the team exactly would collapse the scenario. Team.key is unique per organization, so the description and privacy decoys must carry PAY-like keys (PAYB/PAYS/PAYR) to pass the key check while failing only their own fact — an exact "the PAY team" wording would make them fail the key condition too, and a shared name ("Payments" on five teams) would make an implausible seed. The glob-style "PAY* team" is the most colleague-like phrasing I found for the necessarily loose key match.
